column6: Combinatorial sexual signals: male colour polymorphism, elaborate courtship displays, social learning of mate preferences; sensory drive
column8: Explosive radiation followed by saturation; Lake Victoria/Malawi/Tanganyika cichlids show density-dependent slowdown (Seehausen 2006, Wagner et al. 2012)

column6: Birds-of-paradise: elaborate multi-component displays (plumage, dance, vocalizations) under strong sexual selection; Oscine passerines with vocal learning
column8: Irestedt et al. (2009) found moderate diversification rate; family originated ~24 Mya; more geographic isolation than sexual selection as speciation driver

column6: Túngara frog: combinatorial call (whine + optional chucks) under strong sexual selection; sensory exploitation hypothesis supported
column8: Species-level analysis; call complexity driven by female preference but also increases predation risk

column6: Satin bowerbirds and allies: bower construction, decoration, female choice for bower quality; Oscine passerines with vocal learning
column8: Bowerbirds show moderate diversity; bower-building evolved in parallel in two lineages

column6: Hummingbirds: iridescent plumage, aerial displays, vocal learning (Apodiformes), combinatorial signal space (visual + acoustic + movement)
column8: McGuire et al. (2014) documented an early burst followed by slowdown; diversity-dependent model fits well
